Reddit's weird. The leftists think that Reddit's a right-wing controlled cesspit, and the rightists(?) think that Reddit is a left-wing controlled cesspit, when really the whole thing can be equated to monkeys flinging their own crap at each other.

I always get a kick out of threads where the upper half of the comments contain somebody balking at how disgustingly racist/sexist/whatever Reddit (supposedly) is, while anything that could even be vaguely construed as such has been downvoted into oblivion.

You make it sound like there was some scheme that enabled left-winged internet users to somehow "gain power" over reddit. I think that's just the natural evolution of the core base of reddit users, and I don't think it'll be much different here.

The way I see it is the only way to keep one ideology from taking over is a mutual understanding that both left and right deserve an equal say in the discussion. The reason Reddit seemed so left(or right depending on the sub) was because the mob mentality took such a strong hold. If you said anything that wasn't in line with the majority of the site you got downvoted into oblivion and barrage of negative comments. There's no way to prevent a majority opinion, but we should treat any opinions as a welcome perspective. You can explain why you disagree with somebody without being a huge asshole and making them feel their thoughts are unwanted. This goes for both sides of any issue, we should all meet in the middle. I know this is wishful thinking, but if constructive conversation is what we are going for it's something to at least work towards.
